source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: After{H310} six{H8337} days{H3117}, Yeshua{H3442} took{H3947} Petros, and also Ya'akov{H3290} — in the foreign tongue{H3937}, Jaimi — and Yochanan{H3110} his brother{H251}, and led them{H1980} to a high{H1364} mountain{H2022}, that he might pray{H6419} there.

one_way_hebrew: The ms glosses יעקב with the la'az גאימ״י — Jaimi, the Iberian form of James (Jaime). Like evangeli (24:14) and Kristo (16:16), the gloss runs from the Hebrew name outward to the church's vocabulary, and this one is specifically Spanish — the annotation layer of a Hebrew text read in Sepharad.
greek_deviations: The Hebrew gives the purpose of the ascent: להתפלל — 'to pray.' Greek Matthew and Mark have no prayer here; LUKE does (Luke 9:28, 'he went up into the mountain TO PRAY'). The first of a chain of agreements with Luke running through this whole scene (vv. 2, 3, 4, 7).
translation_notes: אתר — the ms writes אתר for אחר ('after'), a ח/ת interchange of the same kind as תפשים for חפשים in v. 26.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק ע״ג (Perek 73) begins here.

Howard's apparatus (17:1): ששה] ששת ABDEF; לפייטרוס] לפיטרו AH, לפיטרוש BDEG; וגם יעקב] ויעקב ADH; לעז] בלעז B; גאימי] גיאימי B; ויוחנן] וגואן D, וגיואני H; אל הר] להר G; משם] + מאד G, omit H; הוא] omit AH.

verses.translation: And while he was praying{H6419}, he was changed{H8138} before them{H6440}, and the skin{H5785} of his face{H6440} shone{H7160} like the sun{H8121}, and his garments{H4403} were white{H3836} like snow{H7950}.

one_way_hebrew: וקרן עור פניו — 'and the skin of his face shone': Exod 34:29-30 and 35 verbatim (קרן עור פניו), the unique idiom of Moses descending Sinai. The transfiguration is told in the exact consonants of Moses' shining face — with Moses himself about to appear (v. 3). Greek ἔλαμψεν τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ('his face shone') translates the sense and loses the quotation; only in Hebrew is the Moses-typology written into the very words.
לבנים כשלג — 'white as snow': Dan 7:9's Ancient of Days (לבושה כתלג חור) and Isa 1:18.
greek_deviations: 'While he was PRAYING he was changed' — again Luke's frame (Luke 9:29, 'as he prayed, the appearance of his face was altered'); Greek Matthew has 'he was transfigured before them' with no prayer.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (17:2): השתנה] השונה F; ומלבושיו...כשלג] omit H.

verses.translation: Moshe{H4872} and Eliyahu{H452} — speaking{H1696} with him{H5973} — and they told{H5046} Yeshua{H3442} all{H3605} that would befall him{H7136} in Yerushalayim{H3389}. And Petros and his companions{H2270} were fast asleep{H7290} — dozing yet not dozing, awake yet not awake — they saw{H7200} his body{H1480} and the two{H8147} men{H376} with him.

one_way_hebrew: נים ולא נים תיר ולא תיר — 'dozing yet not dozing, awake yet not awake': the Talmud's own idiom for half-sleep (b. Pesachim 120b, נים ולא נים תיר ולא תיר). No Greek text has it or could have it; it is untranslatable rabbinic Hebrew sitting in the middle of the narrative — the surest kind of evidence that the narrative is natively Hebrew.

נרדמים (H7290, radam) — the deep-sleep of Daniel at the vision: 'as he was speaking with me I fell into a deep sleep (נרדמתי) with my face toward the ground' (Dan 8:18; 10:9) — the same scene: heavenly speech, sleeping seer, face to the ground (v. 6).
greek_deviations: The whole verse walks with LUKE against Greek Matthew: the two 'told Yeshua all that would befall him in Yerushalayim' (Luke 9:31, 'spoke of his departure which he was about to accomplish at Jerusalem'); 'Petros and his companions were fast asleep' (Luke 9:32, 'Peter and those with him were weighed down with sleep'); 'they saw... the two men with him' (Luke 9:32, 'they saw his glory and the two men standing with him'). None of this is in Greek Matthew.
Where Luke has 'they saw his GLORY,' the Hebrew reads ראו גופו — 'they saw his BODY' — the waking sight was the man himself, and the two men with him.
textual_notes: The verse opens אליהם משה ואליהו ('to them, Moshe and Eliyahu...') with no verb of appearing; mss ABDEFG supply ונגלו ('and there were revealed'), and Howard's English prints '(were revealed).'
Howard's apparatus (17:3): Beginning] + ונגלו ABDEFG; ופייטרוס] ופיטרוש AB, ופיטרוס DEG, F; שיקראהו] שיקריהו B, שיקרהו D; נרדמים] + מאד ABDEF; גופו] אותו G.

verses.translation: And when they were departing{H1980}, Petros said{H559} to Yeshua{H3442}: It is good{H2896} to be here. Let us make{H6213} here{H6311} three{H7969} tabernacles{H4908} — one{H259} for you, one for Moshe{H4872}, and one for Eloah{H433} — for he did not know{H3045} what{H4100} he was saying{H1696}.

one_way_hebrew: משכנות (H4908, mishkan) — Petros proposes to build tabernacles by the Torah's own word for the dwelling-place (Exod 25:9). Greek σκηναί is the generic tent; the Hebrew carries the Sinai freight — fitting the Moses-scene the whole chapter is quoting.
greek_deviations: 'When they were DEPARTING' — Luke 9:33 again ('as they were parting from him, Peter said...'); Greek Matthew has no departure.
textual_notes: The base ms reads ולאלוה אחד — 'and one for ELOAH' — where the Greek and all parallels have Elijah; mss BDEF read ולאליה and A ולאליהו ('for Eliyahu'), which Howard's English follows ('one for Elijah'). The base reading is a copyist's slip of one letter (אליה/אלוה), but as printed the offer stands 'one for Eloah' — and the narrator's verdict 'he did not know what he was saying' sits hard against it.
Howard's apparatus (17:4): אז] omit A; ליש״ו] + אדוני ABDEF, G; פייטרוס] פיטרו A, פיטרוש BDEG, פיטרוס F; משכנות] משכנים ABDEFG; ולאלוה] ולאליה BDEF, ולאליהו A; פה] כאן AEF; בכאן] omit A.

verses.translation: While he was yet speaking{H1696}, behold{H2009}, a cloud{H6051} covered{H3680} them, and they were greatly{H3966} terrified{H926}; and while they were under{H8478} the cloud they heard{H8085} from the midst{H8432} of the cloud a voice{H6963} speaking and saying{H559}: Behold, this is my son{H1121}, my dear one{H3357}, and my delight{H2656} is in him — him you shall heed{H8085}.

one_way_hebrew: The scene is Sinai's: the cloud COVERS (כסה) as in Exod 24:15-16 ('the cloud covered the mount'), and the voice speaks מתוך הענן — 'from the midst of the cloud' — as YHWH called to Moses מתוך הענן (Exod 24:16; cf. Deut 4:12, 'from the midst of the fire').
בני יקירי — 'my son, my dear one': Jer 31:20's word over Ephraim (הבן יקיר לי — 'is Ephraim my dear son?'). Greek ἀγαπητός ('beloved') flattens יקיר to the stock word.
וחפצי בו — 'my delight is in him': the idiom of Isa 62:4 (חפצי־בה, 'Hephzibah — for YHWH delights in her').

אליו תשמעון — Deut 18:15 verbatim: the prophet like Moses, 'him you shall heed' (אליו תשמעון). The voice from the cloud quotes the Torah's own prophet-like-Moses clause over the one standing beside Moses. Greek ἀκούετε αὐτοῦ translates it; the Hebrew IS it.
textual_notes: The base text has a plain ענן ('a cloud'); mss ADG add צח ('a BRIGHT cloud,' assimilating to Greek φωτεινή) and EF add אחד.
שמעו — the scan of Howard's text reads שמעו ('they heard'); the circulating transcription's שמעה is a typo, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (17:5): הנה¹] omit AF; ענן] + צח ADG, + אחד EF; שכסה] כסה ADEF.

verses.translation: And the disciples{H8527} heard{H8085}, and they fell{H5307} on their faces{H6440} to the ground{H776}, and they feared{H3372} greatly{H3966}.

one_way_hebrew: ויפלו על פניהם ארצה — the posture of Ezek 1:28 and Dan 8:17-18 before the glory; with נרדמים in v. 3, the disciples live Daniel's sequence: vision, terror, face to the ground.
textual_notes: No variants recorded in Howard's apparatus for this verse.

verses.translation: And when the voice{H6963} ceased, Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to them: Arise{H6965}, do not fear{H3372}.

greek_deviations: 'When the voice CEASED' — Luke 9:36's note (ἐν τῷ γενέσθαι τὴν φωνήν, 'when the voice was past'), absent from Greek Matthew. And where Greek Matthew has Yeshua come and TOUCH them, the Hebrew has only his word: Arise, do not fear — the pattern of Dan 10:9-12 ('a hand touched me... he said, fear not' is Daniel's; here the word alone raises them).
translation_notes: נפסק — 'was cut off, ceased' (rabbinic פסק, no biblical Strong's number).
אל — the scan of Howard's text reads אל תיראו; the circulating transcription's על is a typo, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (17:7): קומו] omit C; להם] אליהם ABDEFG; ויאמר] ואומר C.

verses.translation: And they lifted{H5375} their eyes{H5869} and saw{H7200} no one except Yeshua{H3442} alone{H905}.

one_way_hebrew: וישאו עיניהם — 'they lifted their eyes,' the Hebrew narrative formula (Gen 22:4; 18:2); Greek ἐπάραντες τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν is a calque of it.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (17:8): בלבד] לבד EFG.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} came down{H3381} from the mountain{H2022}, and he commanded{H6680} them, saying{H559}: Do not speak{H1696} to any man{H376} of the vision{H4758} which you saw{H7200}, until{H5704} the Son{H1121} of Man{H120} arises{H6965} from death{H4194}.

one_way_hebrew: המראה (H4758) — 'the vision,' Daniel's own word for what he saw and was told to seal (Dan 8:26-27, המראה; 10:1). The command to silence over a מראה until an appointed rising is Daniel's pattern.
וירד... מן ההר — Moses' descent formula (Exod 34:29, ברדת משה מן ההר), closing the Sinai frame the chapter opened at v. 2.
שיקום — 'until the Son of Man ARISES from death' (קום, active, as at 16:21; Hos 6:2); Greek ἐγερθῇ is passive 'is raised.'
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק ע״ד (Perek 74) begins here.

verses.translation: And his disciples{H8527} asked him{H7592}, saying{H559}: Why{H4100} do the sages{H2450} say{H559} that Eliyahu{H452} will come{H935} first{H7223}?

greek_deviations: The disciples cite החכמים — 'the sages' — where Greek Matthew has 'the scribes' (γραμματεῖς). As at 16:1, the Hebrew text knows the rabbinic estate by its own name.
translation_notes: וישאלוהו לו — the verb carries its object suffix and then repeats לו; a native redundancy of spoken Hebrew (cf. Ezek 10:3, בבאו האיש).
שאליה — the ms spells Eliyahu without the final vav here and in v. 11 (אליה).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (17:10): וישאלוהו] וישאלו ABDEFG; שאליה] שאליהו A.

verses.translation: And he answered{H6030} them and said{H559}: Indeed{H551} Eliyahu{H452} will come{H935} and will save{H3467} all{H3605} the world{H5769}.

greek_deviations: 'Eliyahu will come and will SAVE all the world' — Greek Matthew reads 'Elijah comes and will RESTORE (ἀποκαταστήσει) all things.' The Hebrew has יושיע (H3467, the yasha-root of the name ישו״ע): Eliyahu's coming is put in the vocabulary of salvation, not restoration — and Mal 3:23-24, the text behind the sages' expectation, ends with Elijah turning hearts 'lest I come and smite the earth' — a saving of the world indeed. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads 'restore everything' with the Greek; the saving-reading is Shem Tov's own.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (17:11): אליה] אליהו A.

verses.translation: I say{H559} to you that he has already{H3528} come{H935}, and they did not recognize him{H5234}, and they did{H6213} to him according to their pleasure{H7522}. So they will do{H6213} to the Son{H1121} of Man{H120}.

one_way_hebrew: הכירוהו (H5234, nakar) — 'they did not RECOGNIZE him': Joseph's word (Gen 42:8, 'Joseph recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him') — the brother standing unknown before his own. The same verb carried 16:23's charge ('you do not recognize the word of El').
translation_notes: The base ms reads פן יעשו כבן אדם (as it stands, 'lest they do as a son of man' — garbled); mss AEFG read כן ('so'), D וכן, and ADG read בבן ('to the Son'). The translation follows the majority sense — 'so will they do to the Son of Man' — which matches the Greek; Howard's English likewise prints '(So) they will do to the Son of Man.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (17:12): אדם] האדם AEF; כבן] בבן ADG; פן] כן AEFG, וכן D; בו] לו G.

verses.translation: Then{H227} the disciples{H8527} understood{H995} that it was concerning Yochanan{H3110} the Immerser{H2881} that he was speaking{H1696} this.

translation_notes: שבשבל — the ms spells בשביל ('concerning, for the sake of') defectively (בשבל); a medieval Hebrew connective with no biblical Strong's number.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (17:13): שבשבל] omit F; מדבר] אומר G.

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961}, when he came{H935} to the companies{H2274}, a man{H376} came before him{H6440}, kneeling{H3766} on his knees{H1290}.

one_way_hebrew: כורע על ברכיו — 'bowing on his knees': the Hebrew posture-idiom of 1 Kgs 8:54 (Solomon, מכרע על ברכיו) and 2 Chr 6:13; Greek γονυπετῶν is its calque.
translation_notes: על — the scan of Howard's text reads כורע על ברכיו; the circulating transcription dropped על, restored here.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק ע״ה (Perek 75) begins here.

verses.translation: And he said{H559}: My lord{H113}, be gracious to me{H2603} and have pity{H2347} on my son{H1121}, for he is terrified{H1204} by an evil{H7451} spirit{H7307} and is very sick{H2470}; and he gnashes{H2786} his teeth{H8127} and foams at his mouth{H6310}, and falls{H5307} from his full height{H6967} to the ground{H776}, and falls sometimes{H6471} into the fire{H784} and sometimes into the water{H4325}.

one_way_hebrew: נבעת מרוח רעה — 'terrified by an evil spirit': the exact pair of Saul's affliction, רוח רעה + בעת ('an evil spirit from YHWH terrified him,' 1 Sam 16:14-15, ובעתתו). Greek Matthew says σεληνιάζεται — 'he is moonstruck' (lunatic) — a pagan astrological diagnosis; the Hebrew diagnoses with Scripture's own case, Saul's.
חנני (H2603) — the Psalter's plea (Ps 6:3, חנני יהוה כי אמלל אני — 'be gracious to me, for I languish... my bones are terrified,' נבהלו); וחוסה — the pity-verb of Joel 2:17 and Jonah 4:11.
translation_notes: ומקטף — so the base ms (ms C's reading, from קטף 'pluck'); mss ABDEFG read ומקצף ('and foams,' cf. קצף, foam, Hos 10:7), which the sense requires — Howard's English prints '(foams) at his mouth.' The translation follows the sense.
וחוסה — the scan of Howard's text reads וחוסה; the circulating transcription's והוסה is a typo, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (17:15): ויאמר] + לו G; חנני] חנינו B, חונני G; וחוסה] וחוס EF; מאד] עד מאד G; את] על B; ומקטף] ומקצף ABDEFG; ונופל פעמים] ופעמים נופל ABDEFG.

verses.translation: And I brought him{H935} to your disciples{H8527}, but they were not able{H3201} to heal him{H7495}.

translation_notes: לתלמידך — the consonants read either 'to your disciple' (singular) or defectively 'to your disciples'; mss ADEF write לתלמידיך in full, and Howard renders 'to your disciple(s).'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (17:16): והביאותיו] והבאתיו ADEF; לתלמידך] לתלמידיך ADEF; יוכלו] יכלו ADEF; לרפאתו] לרפאותו ADEF.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} answered{H6030} and said{H559}: Evil{H7451} generation{H1755}! Woe{H188} to you, you deniers — until{H5704} when{H4970} shall I be with you{H5973}, and until when shall I bear{H5375} your trouble{H2960}? Bring him{H935} to me.

one_way_hebrew: עד מתי אשא טרחכם — Moses' own words: 'How can I bear alone your trouble (אשא... טרחכם)' (Deut 1:12); and God's in Isa 1:14 ('they are a TROUBLE — טרח — to me; I am weary of BEARING them — נשא'). טרח occurs only in those two places in Scripture, and the Hebrew Matthew uses both of their verbs. Greek 'how long shall I put up with you (ἀνέξομαι)' has none of it — the prophet-like-Moses (v. 5, אליו תשמעון) here speaks Moses' sentence.
הכופרים — kofrim, 'the deniers': the rabbinic category (kofer ba-ikkar, the denier of the root). Greek has ἄπιστος ('faithless'); the Hebrew uses the working Jewish term for those who deny.
greek_deviations: Greek Matthew: 'O faithless and perverse generation.' The Hebrew: 'Evil generation! Woe to you, you deniers.' Mss ABDEFG rearrange to אוי דור רע וכופר ('Woe, evil and denying generation'), assimilating toward the Greek shape; the base text keeps the direct woe-address.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (17:17): דור רע אוי לכם] transposed (אוי דור רע) ABDEFG; לכם אתם] omit ABDEFG; הכופרים] וכופר ABDEFG.

verses.translation: And they brought him{H935} to him, and immediately, when Yeshua{H3442} looked at him{H7200}, the satan{H7854} subdued him{H3665} and cast him{H5307} to the ground{H776}, and he began{H2490} rolling in the dust{H6080} and foaming{H7107}. And Yeshua asked{H7592} the father{H1} of the boy{H5288}: How much{H4100} time{H2165} has the satan taken him{H3947}? And the father answered him{H7725}: From a certain{H6423} time and onward{H1973}. And many{H7235} times{H6471} he has cast him{H5307} into the fire{H784} and into the water{H4325}, so that he might destroy him{H8045}. And if you, my lord{H113}, are able{H3201} in any way{H6045} to help him{H5826} — help him! And the man{H376} found{H5375} favor{H2580} in his eyes{H5869}, and he was filled{H4390} with compassion{H7356} for him. And he said{H559} to him: If you can{H3201} believe{H539}, you will be able to accomplish{H7999} anything{H1697}, for to the believer{H539} all{H3605} things{H1697} are light{H7031}. And immediately the father{H1} of the boy{H5288} wept{H1058} with a cry{H6818} and said: My lord{H113}, I believe{H539}; indeed{H551}, help me{H5826} according to my faith{H530}. And when Yeshua{H3442} saw{H7200} that the people{H5971} were gathering{H6908}, he said{H559} to him: Strong{H2389} and mute{H483} one! Behold, I command you{H6680}: come out{H3318} from here — and from now onward{H1973} you shall not return{H7725} here again{H5750}. And the satan{H7854} went out{H3318} screaming{H6817} and inflicting pain{H3510}, and the boy{H5288} was left{H7604} as dead{H4191}, so that many{H7227} were saying{H559} that he was dead{H4191}. And Yeshua{H3442} took him{H3947} and stood him up{H5975}, and he arose{H6965}.

one_way_hebrew: וישא האיש חן בעיניו — 'the man found favor in his eyes': the covenant idiom of Gen 6:8 (Noach מצא חן בעיני יהוה) and Esth 5:2 (נשאה חן בעיניו). This narrative clause — the father finds favor, and Yeshua is filled with compassion (ונתמלא רחמים) — is in no Greek text of Mark or Matthew; it is the Hebrew narrator's own sentence, told in Hebrew narrative formulas.
מתעפר — 'rolling in the dust' (עפר): the gesture-word of Shimei hurling dust (2 Sam 16:13, ועפר בעפר). Greek Mark's ἐκυλίετο ('wallowed') is generic; the Hebrew names the dust.

מזמן פלוני — 'from such-and-such a time': פלוני (H6423) is the Tanakh's own placeholder word (Ruth 4:1, פלני אלמני; 1 Sam 21:3). Greek Mark has 'from childhood' (παιδιόθεν) — the Hebrew answer is the native idiom of unspecified reference.
greek_deviations: The famous cry of Greek Mark 9:24 — 'Lord, I believe; help thou mine UNBELIEF' — reads here: 'My lord, I believe; indeed, help me ACCORDING TO MY FAITH (עוזרני לפי אמונתי).' The father does not confess unbelief; he asks to be helped in the measure of the faith he has. The whole paradox the Greek is famous for is absent from the Hebrew.

The address to the spirit is חזק ואלם — 'strong and mute one' — where Greek Mark has 'mute and DEAF spirit.' And the expulsion is permanent by command: 'from now onward you shall not return here again' (cf. Mark's 'enter no more into him').

'If you can believe, you will be able to accomplish anything, for to the believer all things are LIGHT (קלים)' — Greek Mark: 'all things are POSSIBLE (δυνατά) to him that believes.' The Hebrew says the burden grows light, not that the impossible opens.
translation_notes: ומיד — the scan of Howard's text reads ומיד ('and immediately'); the circulating transcription's ומיעד is a typo, corrected here. Likewise בעניין (transcription העניין), לעוזרו (transcription לאוזרו), and מכאן ומכאן (the transcription dropped one מכאן).
אדו׳ — the ms abbreviates אדון/אדוני with a geresh, here and in the father's cry.
textual_notes: THE MS PLACES THE FULLER MARK-PARALLEL NARRATIVE HERE. Where Greek Matthew has only 17:18 ('And Yeshua rebuked him, and the demon went out of him, and the boy was healed from that hour'), the Shem Tov text carries the whole healing as the longer narrative Greek readers know from Mark 9:20-27 — the fall, the father's history, the dialogue on faith, the command, the corpse-like boy raised. Howard labels these verses 'MK 9:20-27' and sets them off with a [MARK] divider; they are encoded here as one entry under verse 18, whose content they carry. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew has only the short Matthean form ('Yeshua rebuked the satan, and he went out, and the young man was cleansed in that hour') — the fuller narrative is Shem Tov's own.
Howard's apparatus (MK 9:20): והביאוהו] ויבאוהו A; והביאוהו...השטן] ומה שהביאוהו אליו וישו ראה השטן G; ומפילו] והפילו G.
Howard's apparatus (MK 9:21): זמן] + יש ABDEFG; והאב] ואביו AG; והלאה] + ומיד ABDEFG.
Howard's apparatus (MK 9:22): אדון] אדוני A; השמידו] להשמידו ABDEFG; יוכל] יכול A, שיוכל G; לעוזרו] לעזרו ABCDEFG; עזרהו] עזרנו ABDEF; וישא] וישו A; בעיניו] ביעיניו F.
Howard's apparatus (MK 9:23): אם] + אתה ABDEFG; הדברים] + אצלו ABDEFG ('all things are easy TO HIM'); קלים] קלה BDEFG.
Howard's apparatus (MK 9:24): בצעקה] omit G; אדון] אדוני A, omit B.

Howard's apparatus (MK 9:25): לזה] צוה לשד ABDEFG ('he commanded the demon' — Howard's English follows: '(he commanded the demon)'); לו] + שטן A; מכאן ומכאן] מבטן ומבטן DG ('from the womb'); ראה] omit G.
Howard's apparatus (MK 9:26): שהוא מת] שמת הוא ABDEF, מה הוא G; יצא] היה C.
Howard's apparatus (MK 9:27): לקחו] + מהיד ABDG, מיד EF ('took him by the hand,' assimilating to Mark — Howard's English: 'took him (by the hand)'); והעמידו] והעמידוהו B.

verses.translation: And when Yeshua{H3442} entered{H3664} the house{H1004}, then{H227} the disciples{H8527} drew near{H7126} to Yeshua in secret{H5643} and said{H559} to him: Why{H4069} were we{H587} not able{H3201} to cast him out{H3318}?

greek_deviations: The house is Mark's: Greek Matthew 17:19 has only 'the disciples came to Yeshua privately'; Greek Mark 9:28 has 'when he had come into the house, his disciples asked him privately.' The Hebrew carries both clauses in one breath — the ms runs the Markan house-notice (which Howard labels MK 9:28) directly into Matthew's verse, and it is encoded here as the opening of v. 19.
textual_notes: Howard prints וכאשר נכנס יש״ו לבית under the label MK 9:28, followed by a [MATTHEW] divider before this verse; the clause is folded into the start of this entry, where its scene belongs.
ויאמרו — the scan of Howard's text reads ויאמרו ('and they said'); the circulating transcription's ויאמר is corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (MK 9:28): וכאשר] + עמד G. Howard's apparatus (17:19): קרבו] + לו A; בסתר] omit AF; מדוע] למה G; אליו] לו A.

verses.translation: And he said{H559} to them: Because of the littleness{H4592} of your faith{H530}. Amen{H543}, I say{H559} to you: if there be in you any of the faith{H530}, as a grain{H1620} of mustard — if you believe{H539} — you will say{H559} to this{H2088} mountain{H2022}: Depart{H5493}! and it will depart; and nothing{H1697} will be withheld{H1219} from you.

one_way_hebrew: וכל דבר לא יבצר מכם — Gen 11:6 verbatim: 'and now nothing will be withheld from them (לא יבצר מהם) which they have purposed to do' — the sentence spoken over Babel's builders, here turned right-side up over believers. Greek οὐδὲν ἀδυνατήσει ὑμῖν ('nothing will be impossible for you') translates the sense and loses the quotation. Only the Hebrew reader hears that faith receives what Babel grasped at.

כגרגיר חרדל — 'as a grain of mustard': גרגיר (H1620) is Isa 17:6's word for the last berries on the olive tree, and 'a grain of mustard' (חרדל) is the rabbis' own smallest-measure idiom (כעין החרדל); the phrase is native Jewish measurement-speech.
translation_notes: חרדל — mustard; a rabbinic-Hebrew word with no biblical Strong's number.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (17:20): ויאמר] אמר EF; להם] אליהם AB; תאמינו] omit A; להר הזה תאמרו] transposed AEF; סורו] סור ABEFG.

verses.translation: And this{H2088} kind{H4327} of the demons{H7700} does not come out{H3318} except by prayer{H8605} and fasting{H6685}.

one_way_hebrew: השדים (H7700, shedim) — the Torah's own demon-word (Deut 32:17, 'they sacrificed to shedim, not to Eloah'); Greek δαιμόνιον is the pagan loan-category, שד the covenant one.
המין (H4327, min) — 'kind, species': Genesis 1's sorting word (למינו), applied here to the demonic orders.
greek_deviations: Greek Matthew 17:21 is missing from the earliest Greek witnesses (א* B and others omit it; many hold it was carried in from Mark 9:29). The Hebrew text has the verse without question — no Shem Tov ms lacks it.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (17:21): מן השדים] מהשדים A.

verses.translation: While they were in Galil{H1551}, Yeshua{H3442} said{H559}: The Son{H1121} of Man{H120} will be delivered{H4560} into the hand{H3027} of the sons{H1121} of man{H120}.

one_way_hebrew: בן האדם ימסר ליד בני האדם — 'the SON OF MAN delivered into the hand of the SONS OF MAN': in Hebrew the betrayal is written as one word given into the hands of its own plural — an irony exact and complete. Greek must switch words (ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου... εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων) and the edge dulls.

ימסר (H4560, masar) — the handing-over verb of Num 31:5,16; in rabbinic Hebrew the mosér is the one who delivers a fellow Jew over — the Hebrew word carries the traitor's shadow that Greek παραδίδοσθαι only points at.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק ע״ו (Perek 76) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (17:22): האדם¹] אדם ABDEFG.

verses.translation: And they will kill him{H2026}, and on the third{H7992} day{H3117} he will arise{H6965}.

one_way_hebrew: וביום השלישי יקום — Hos 6:2 again ('on the third day he will raise us up'), as at 16:21; the Hebrew keeps Hosea's active verb where Greek has the passive 'be raised.'
greek_deviations: Greek Matthew ends the verse 'and they were exceedingly sorry' (καὶ ἐλυπήθησαν σφόδρα); the Hebrew has no grief-clause — the announcement stands alone. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew carries the clause ('and they were exceedingly anxious') with the Greek; its absence is Shem Tov's own.
textual_notes: No variants recorded in Howard's apparatus for this verse.

verses.translation: And they came{H935} to Kefar{H3723} Nachum{H5151} Martah, and the receivers{H6901} of the tax{H4371} drew near{H7126} to Petros and said{H559}: Your rabbi does not customarily{H5090} give{H5414} the tax{H4371}.

one_way_hebrew: מכס (H4371) — the tax by the Torah's own levy-word (Num 31:28-41, the מכס rendered to YHWH from the spoil); Greek has the Greek coin δίδραχμα. A Hebrew author names the institution, a Greek one the currency.
כפר נחום — Capernaum resolved into its Hebrew parts, 'the village of Nachum'; the Greek Καφαρναούμ is a transliteration of exactly this.
רביכם — 'your rabbi': the living title (cf. רבי throughout rabbinic literature); Greek ὁ διδάσκαλος ὑμῶν translates it.
greek_deviations: The collectors make a statement, not a question: 'Your rabbi does not customarily give the tax' — an accusation. Greek Matthew has the polite question 'Does not your teacher pay the didrachma?'
translation_notes: מרתה — an obscure addition to the place-name; Howard renders 'Capernaum-Martha.' Ms A reads רמתה ('toward Ramah'?). The word is left as the ms gives it.
המכס — the scan of Howard's text reads המכס; the circulating transcription's המכם is a typo, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (17:24): לפייטרוס] לפיטרו A, לפיטרוש BDEFG; ויקרבוהו] ויקרבו ABCDEFG; מרתה] רמתה A; נוהג ונותן] נותן ABDEFG; אליהם] אליו A.

verses.translation: And they said{H559}: Yes{H3651}. And when they came{H935} into the house{H1004}, Yeshua{H3442} anticipated him{H6923}, saying{H559} to Petros: What{H4100} seems right{H7200} to you, Petros — the kings{H4428} of the earth{H776}, from whom{H4310} do they take{H3947} tax{H4371}: from their sons{H1121}, or from the strangers{H5237}?

one_way_hebrew: מלכי ארץ — 'the kings of the earth': Ps 2:2's phrase (מלכי ארץ), the kings arrayed against YHWH and his anointed — and the question is precisely whether the Anointed's household owes them tribute.
והקדים — 'he anticipated him' (קדם, H6923, the psalmists' fore-meeting verb, Ps 119:147-148); Greek προέφθασεν translates the same idiom.
הנכרים (H5237, nokri) — the Torah's own word for the outsider as against the son (Deut 17:15).
translation_notes: בניהם — the scan of Howard's text reads בניהם ('their sons'); the circulating transcription's נביהם is a letter-swap typo, corrected here.
לאמר אליו לפייט״רוס — the doubled indirect object ('to him, to Petros') is the ms's own colloquial fullness.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (17:25): ויבואו] ויבא A; בבית] בביתו G; לאמר אליו] transposed ABCDEFG; פייטרוס] פיטרו AD, פיטרוש BEFG, פיטרוס C; נראה] יראה ABDEFG; מלכי...הנכרים] omit C.

verses.translation: And he answered{H6030} him: From the strangers{H5237}. And Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to them: If so{H3651}, the sons{H1121} are free. And he said: You shall not be alarmed{H926} on account{H5668} of this —

one_way_hebrew: 'The sons are free' — the argument runs on the Hebrew בנים just used of Israel's kings' sons: the King's own sons owe no מכס. The Hebrew reader has heard בן האדם delivered to בני האדם (v. 22) and now hears whose sons are free of the earth's kings.
translation_notes: תפשים — the base ms writes תפשים (as the letters stand, 'seized'); mss ABDEFG read חפשים ('free'), which the sense requires — a ח/ת interchange exactly like אתר for אחר in v. 1. Howard's English prints '(free).' The translation follows the sense.

לא תהיו בעבר זה נבהלים — 'you shall not be alarmed over this': where Greek Matthew has 'lest we cause them to stumble (σκανδαλίσωμεν),' the Hebrew's concern is the disciples' own composure — pay, and be untroubled.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (17:26): להם] אליהם A; תפשים] חפשים ABDEFG.

verses.translation: and he said{H559} to Petros: Go{H1980} to the sea{H3220} and cast{H7993} a hook{H2443}, and that fish{H1709} which you take{H3947} first{H7223} — you will find{H4672} in its mouth{H6310} a coin of silver{H3701}, and it you shall give{H5414} for us{H1157}.

one_way_hebrew: חכה (H2443) — the fish-hook of Isa 19:8 ('the fishers... all they that cast hook into the Nile'), Hab 1:15, and Job 40:25 ('can you draw out Leviathan with a hook?'). Greek ἄγκιστρον translates the same rare word. The whole command is built of Tanakh fishing vocabulary — חכה, דג, ים.
greek_deviations: Greek Matthew names the coin twice over — a στατήρ found 'instead of me and you' (ἀντὶ ἐμοῦ καὶ σοῦ). The Hebrew has simply 'a coin of silver... give it בעדינו — for us' — one word covering master and disciple together, with no Greek coinage named (mss ABDEFG read בצע, 'a piece of money,' for מטבע).
translation_notes: מטבע — 'coin,' the rabbinic-Hebrew word (matbea'), with no biblical Strong's number — the author's living vocabulary, as at 16:26.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (17:27): לפייטרוס] לפיטרו A, לפיטרוש BDEFG, לפיטרוס C; שתקח] שתצר G; תמצא] ומצא EF, שתמצא G(?); מטבע] בצע ABDEFG; בעדינו] בעדנו DEF.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 17 in the Shem Tov Hebrew is the Moses-chapter told in Moses' own words, and it carries the book's largest structural surprise. (1) 17:2 reads וקרן עור פניו — 'the skin of his face shone' — Exod 34:29-30 verbatim: the transfiguration is written in the exact consonants of Moses' descent from Sinai, and the voice from the cloud (v. 5) speaks Deut 18:15 verbatim — אליו תשמעון, 'him you shall heed' — with Jer 31:20's בני יקירי ('my dear son') before it. The cloud covers (כסה) and speaks 'from the midst of the cloud' as at Exod 24:15-16. (2) The scene walks with LUKE against Greek Matthew at point after point: Yeshua ascends TO PRAY (Luke 9:28) and is changed WHILE PRAYING (9:29); Moshe and Eliyahu tell him 'all that would befall him in Yerushalayim' (9:31); Petros and his companions are asleep and see 'the two men with him' (9:32); Petros speaks 'as they were departing' (9:33); the voice 'ceased' (9:36). (3) The disciples' half-sleep is described in the Talmud's own untranslatable idiom — נים ולא נים תיר ולא תיר (b. Pesachim 120b). (4) Between 17:17 and 17:19 the ms carries the epileptic-boy healing in its fuller Mark 9:20-27 form (Howard labels it MK 9:20-27 with a [MARK] divider; encoded here under v. 18): in it the father's cry is 'help me ACCORDING TO MY FAITH' — no 'help my unbelief' — and the Hebrew narrator adds 'the man found favor in his eyes (Gen 6:8's idiom), and he was filled with compassion.' The Markan house-notice (MK 9:28) then opens v. 19. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew has only the short Matthean healing — the insertion is Shem Tov's own. (5) 17:17 answers with Moses' own sentence: עד מתי אשא טרחכם — 'how long shall I bear your trouble' (Deut 1:12, אשא... טרחכם; Isa 1:14) — and calls the generation כופרים, the rabbinic word for deniers. (6) 17:20's promise quotes Gen 11:6 verbatim — 'nothing will be withheld (לא יבצר) from you' — Babel's sentence turned over to faith. (7) 17:11 reads 'Eliyahu will come and will SAVE all the world' (יושיע) where Greek has 'restore.' (8) 17:22's prophecy is a pure Hebrew pun — בן האדם delivered into the hands of בני האדם — and 17:23 lacks Greek Matthew's 'and they were exceedingly sorry.' (9) 17:24-27 run on Torah institutions: the tax is מכס (Num 31:28), the collectors approach 'your rabbi,' the kings are מלכי ארץ (Ps 2:2), and the coin is found for 'us' (בעדינו) with no stater named. (10) 17:15 diagnoses the boy with Saul's affliction — נבעת מרוח רעה, 'terrified by an evil spirit' (1 Sam 16:14-15) — where Greek says 'moonstruck.' Shem Tov's section divisions fall at vv. 1 (Perek 73), 9 (74), 14 (75), and 22 (76).
